I was born in Kolkata, West Bengal, India. I especially appreciate the hands-on workbook as well as the live classes. On a personal note, I have been able to manage time better, stay focused for a disciplined lifestyle, and value integrity at every step. I have connected with my mentors and fellow students on LinkedIn and stay in touch with quite a few of them—especially when it comes to sharing ideas and knowledge and the zeal to kickstart something in this AI domain. The sort of networking also stands out, as I feel fortunate to team up with some brilliant minds, which includes my mentors as well as fellow batchmates. Nashik, I am currently working in a law college as an Assistant Professor, and my age is 49. My total work experience in teaching and research is 18 years. I hold an M.Sc in Zoology, an M.Phil, a Ph.D. in Genotoxicity, an LLM, an MD (EH), an ND, and I pursued the PGPDSBA from the University of Texas at Great Austin while working as an Assistant Professor at a Science and Law College. My early career aspirations were rooted in the life sciences, with a strong focus on teaching and research in fields like genetics, microbiology, and environmental toxicology. During my PhD, I conducted in-depth gene transcriptome analysis to study the genotoxic effects of pesticides on Drosophila species, and this work exposed me to large-scale biological data and sparked a keen interest in the potential of computational tools for deeper insights. Over time, I realized that combining life sciences with data science and artificial intelligence could unlock new avenues for impactful research, and this realization led me to pursue upskilling in AI, machine learning, and big data analytics—marking a significant shift and evolution in my career path toward interdisciplinary innovation. A turning point came during my PhD research when I was analyzing large-scale gene transcriptome data, and I realized that to truly understand and interpret complex biological patterns, I needed advanced data analysis and computational skills. This realization motivated me to upskill in AI, machine learning, and big data to enhance my research and open new career avenues. Initially, my family and friends were surprised and a bit skeptical about my decision to shift from a life science background to learning AI and data science, however, as they saw my dedication and progress—especially handling coding and complex data—they became supportive and proud of the transformation I achieved through continuous learning. My biggest supporter has been my family, who always encouraged my passion for learning and stood by me during every phase—whether it was pursuing a PhD or transitioning into the field of data science. I chose this specific program by Deakin University and Great Learning because it offered a perfect blend of academic rigor and practical application, and the structured curriculum, industry-relevant projects, dedicated mentorship, and flexibility for working professionals made it stand out among other options in the market. It felt like the right fit to bridge my life science background with data science skills. My learning experience was truly transformative; coming from a non-technical background, I initially found concepts like artificial intelligence, mathematics for AI, and engineering AI solutions quite intimidating, but the program's well-structured tutorials, hands-on assignments, and consistent mentor support made these complex topics approachable. I gradually built confidence in areas like data wrangling, model building, and understanding the foundations of modern data science. Each module not only strengthened my technical skills but also gave me real-world exposure through projects that made learning highly practical and relevant. It was a challenging journey, but one that empowered me to apply these skills confidently in interdisciplinary domains. I enjoyed several aspects of the program, but what stood out the most were the mentor-led sessions that made complex topics like AI, machine learning, and mathematics for AI easier to understand, and the hands-on assignments and real-world projects were incredibly engaging and helped me apply theoretical concepts in a practical way. I particularly enjoyed working on data wrangling, engineering AI solutions, and exploring modern data science tools. Another highlight was the exposure to Microsoft Azure, where I learned how to implement AI and data science solutions on cloud platforms—an essential skill in today’s tech landscape. The program’s flexibility also made it easier to balance learning with my professional commitments, making the experience even more rewarding. Through the program, I developed several tangible skills such as Python programming, data wrangling, machine learning, mathematics for AI, engineering AI solutions, and working with cloud platforms like Microsoft Azure, and I also gained hands-on experience with data visualization, big data tools, and model deployment techniques. On the intangible side, I developed strong problem-solving abilities, analytical thinking, and the confidence to work in interdisciplinary teams. I also became more resilient, curious, and open to continuous learning—skills that are essential in the ever-evolving tech landscape. Coming from a life science background, one of the biggest challenges was understanding mathematics for AI, coding in Python, and grasping machine learning concepts without any prior exposure, and initially, it felt overwhelming to keep up with the technical pace. However, I overcame these hurdles through consistent practice, actively participating in mentor sessions, revisiting tutorial videos, and completing hands-on assignments. The structured guidance and support from mentors helped me break down complex topics into manageable parts, and gradually, everything started to make sense. With time and persistence, I turned my weaknesses into strengths. Overall, the program was well-structured and highly effective, but a few areas could be improved. I would have appreciated more beginner-friendly resources for non-technical learners, especially in the early modules covering math and programming basics, and additional live coding sessions or weekly doubt-clearing webinars could have made the learning curve smoother. Also, more industry-specific case studies, especially related to life sciences or healthcare, would have made the application of AI even more relatable for learners from diverse backgrounds like mine. The skills I gained from the program have been directly applicable to my academic and research work, and a key example is during the analysis of gene transcriptome data in my PhD research on genotoxicity in Drosophila. After learning Python, data wrangling, and machine learning techniques, I was able to streamline the data processing pipeline, perform advanced statistical analysis, and generate more meaningful visualizations. These improvements not only enhanced the quality of my research but also reduced the time spent on manual analysis. The ability to integrate AI and data science tools into my life science research was a game-changer, opening doors for interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation. One of the most unexpected benefits was discovering my ability to learn and excel in technical subjects like AI and programming, and I also found that my domain knowledge in biology and genetics became a unique advantage when applying data science to research problems. Another surprise was the network of like-minded peers and mentors I built during the program, which offered valuable support and insights. Beyond technical skills, I developed a growth mindset, improved my problem-solving approach, and gained the confidence to take on interdisciplinary challenges I once thought were beyond my reach. Acquiring skills in AI, machine learning, big data, and cloud platforms like Azure has significantly expanded my career opportunities, and I can now confidently explore interdisciplinary roles that merge life sciences with data science, such as bioinformatics, healthcare analytics, and AI-driven research. These skills have made me more competitive in both academic and industry settings. Beyond the technical skills, the journey brought immense personal growth—I developed a growth mindset, stronger self-discipline, and the confidence to step outside my comfort zone. I became more resilient, better at managing time, and more open to continuous learning—qualities that have not only advanced my career but also enriched me personally. One valuable connection I made during the program was with a mentor who had transitioned from a core engineering background into AI for healthcare, and their insights into bridging technical knowledge with domain expertise deeply resonated with my own journey from life sciences into data science. They guided me on how to approach interdisciplinary problems, refine my project ideas, and even shared research trends in AI applications for genomics and healthcare. This connection not only provided mentorship but also inspired new career possibilities and collaborative thinking beyond the classroom. Following my upskilling journey, I aspire to work at the intersection of life sciences and artificial intelligence, contributing to impactful research and innovation in areas like genomics, precision medicine, and healthcare analytics. I aim to apply AI and machine learning to solve real-world biological problems and eventually take on roles in bioinformatics, AI research, or data-driven public health projects. I’m also passionate about continuing academic contributions and mentoring others from non-technical backgrounds who wish to transition into the tech-driven future of science. The moment that stands out the most was when I successfully built and deployed my first machine learning model to analyze biological data during one of the capstone projects. Coming from a non-technical background, seeing my code work and generate meaningful results felt like a major breakthrough—it was the moment I truly realized that I had overcome my initial fears of mathematics and programming, and that I was capable of solving complex problems using AI and data science. That success was both empowering and unforgettable. Before the program, my career was rooted in life sciences, medical science, and law, and while I had strong domain knowledge, I felt limited when it came to exploring opportunities in the rapidly evolving data-driven landscape. I lacked technical skills in areas like coding, mathematics for AI, and data analytics, which made it challenging to bridge my expertise with emerging technologies. After completing the program, my life has transformed both personally and professionally. I now feel confident working with AI, machine learning, big data, and cloud platforms like Azure, and can apply these skills to interdisciplinary domains—including genomics, healthcare analytics, and even legal tech. The program empowered me to merge my knowledge of medical science and law with modern data science practices, opening doors to unique career paths in AI-driven research, digital health, and legal data analysis. It has also strengthened my adaptability, critical thinking, and lifelong learning mindset—qualities that continue to guide my evolving journey. My advice is simple: don’t let your background define your limits. Whether you're from life sciences, law, or any non-technical field, it's never too late to step into the world of AI, machine learning, and data science. With the right guidance, structured learning, and consistent effort, even the most complex subjects become manageable. Be patient with yourself, embrace the learning curve, and make the most of mentor support, hands-on projects, and peer discussions. The transformation you experience will not only open new career doors but also boost your confidence in unimaginable ways. If I could make this shift, so can you—just start, stay committed, and trust the process. As a proud alumnus of the Post Graduate Diploma in Management (PGDM) program at Great Lakes Institute of Management and a brand ambassador for this esteemed institution, I am thrilled to share my transformative journey that has not only shaped my career but also redefined my aspirations. Graduating in 2025, I secured a coveted role as a Consultant at Capgemini, with an extraordinary pay scale increment of over 85%. This milestone is a testament to the unparalleled academic rigor, industry- relevant curriculum, and exceptional career support provided by Great Lakes Institute of Management and its partner, Great Learning. The PGDM program at Great Lakes stands out for its world-class faculty, many of whom are distinguished alumni of IITs and IIMs. Their expertise, coupled with a passion for teaching, brought complex business concepts to life through engaging lectures and practical insights. The curriculum was enriched with globally recognized case studies from Harvard and other premier sources, which challenged us to think critically and solve real-world business problems. Projects like Karmayoga and Capstones were game-changers, allowing me to apply theoretical knowledge to practical scenarios, honing my analytical and decision-making skills while fostering a sense of social responsibility and innovation. Great Lakes’ commitment to holistic development extended beyond academics. The Career Mentorship Program provided personalized guidance, helping me align my goals with industry expectations. The CV Review Sessions were instrumental in crafting a professional resume that highlighted my strengths, while the Excelerate Placement Portal streamlined the placement process, connecting me with top-tier recruiters like Capgemini. These initiatives, combined with mock interviews and industry interaction sessions, equipped me with the confidence and skills to excel in the competitive corporate landscape. Great Learning, as a partner, amplified this experience by offering cutting-edge resources and industry-aligned learning modules. Their focus on emerging technologies and data-driven decision-making complemented the PGDM curriculum, ensuring I was well-prepared for the demands of a consulting role at Capgemini. The synergy between Great Lakes and Great Learning created a dynamic learning ecosystem that bridged academia and industry seamlessly. The placement process was a reflection of Great Lakes’ strong industry connect and reputation. Securing a role at Capgemini with such a significant salary hike was beyond my expectations and a direct outcome of the institute’s rigorous training and personalized support. The faculty, mentors, and placement team worked tirelessly to ensure every student was positioned for success, making the transition from classroom to boardroom smooth and rewarding.
